The growth rate of a gallbladder polyp can provide some insight into whether it may be neoplastic. However, several factors need to be considered in determining if this information is reliable.

Patient's age (>60 y) and large polyp size (>10 mm) were significant predictive factors for neoplastic GB polyps. While being over 60 years old and having a large polyp size can increase the risk of a gallbladder polyp becoming cancerous, these factors alone do not guarantee that a specific polyp will become cancerous.

GB polyps less than 10 mm in diameter do not require surgical intervention simply because they grow. This is because the majority of small gallbladder polyps (less than 1 cm) are benign and do not cause symptoms or lead to serious complications.

It's essential to note that predicting whether a gallbladder polyp will become cancerous based solely on growth rate is not always reliable. Other factors, such as the patient's overall health, lifestyle, and family history of cancer, should also be taken into account when making decisions about treatment or surveillance.

In summary, while the growth rate of a gallbladder polyp can provide some information about its potential risk of becoming cancerous, it is not a reliable predictor on its own. Additional factors should be considered in determining the best course of action for each individual patient.
